areas for afforestation and reforestation based on the regulations set by 
the UNFCCC and Ministry of Forestry (MoFE 2015). Afforested areas 
were defined as non-forested regions of > 50 years. However, owing to 
data limitations, an adjusted approach was adopted in which the target 
areas for afforestation were identified by integrating non-forested

impervious surface data from 1983 to 2000 (Gong et al., 2020), and

quote: Where forests are recovering on unused agricultural land, global forces, such as market shifts in the prices of forest-risk commodities (for example, cattle, coffee, cacao or palm oil) can push landholders to reclear land if com- modities become more valuable.
At local levels, young regenerating forests are often perceived as unused or wasteland, and may be recleared to claim or retain control of land44.

In many countries, national policies aimed at protecting forests by imposing use or clearing restrictions on forests of a certain age, height or area can create perverse incen- tives to prevent forests from regrowing if landholders seek to retain control of their land43.
Naturally regenerating forests do not fit into many current categories for carbon offsetting46.
